questions.q: In this capstone's scenario, what is the Business Service?
options: Patient Scheduling Application Service
The Electronic Health Records (EHR) platform
Patient Scheduling
Meridian Regional Health
questions.explain: Patient Scheduling is the Business Service — what patients and schedulers experience, and what leadership means when they ask whether it's up. Patient Scheduling Application Service is the Technical Service underneath it.

questions.q: Why is Patient Scheduling Application Service modeled as a Technical Service rather than as the Business Service itself?
options: Technical Services are only used when a system has no database
It's the layer made of real, physical and virtual infrastructure — servers, a database, a load balancer, the application — that the Business Service depends on
Technical Services don't appear anywhere in CSDM
There is no meaningful difference between the two layers
questions.explain: Chapter 3's split puts the infrastructure-backed layer in the Technical Service; the Business Service is the business-facing layer on top of it.

questions.q: What is explicitly out of scope for this capstone, and why?
options: All four of Meridian's hospitals, because the capstone only covers one hospital
The EHR platform's own infrastructure, because it's already its own Business Service with its own owner and CMDB footprint elsewhere
The scheduling application itself, because it will be modeled in a later course
Nothing is out of scope — this capstone models the entire hospital's IT estate
questions.explain: The EHR platform is excluded by design. This capstone adds only one relationship showing the handoff point, rather than re-modeling the EHR's infrastructure.

questions.q: Why does drawing an explicit scope boundary before creating any CI matter, per this lesson and Chapter 1 Lesson 3?
options: It doesn't matter — scope can always be decided after the CIs exist
Scope boundaries are only needed for Discovery, not for manually created CIs
Without one, a first CMDB build risks sprawling into a half-finished mess of records nobody maintains
A scope boundary is a ServiceNow table, not a planning decision
questions.explain: Chapter 1 Lesson 3 covered this directly: trying to model everything at once is how CMDBs end up bloated with records nobody keeps current.

questions.q: What is the correct order of this capstone's four-lesson plan?
options: Governance plan, then build CIs, then apply CSDM, then scope the service
Scope the service, build CIs and relationships, apply CSDM and validate data quality, then write the governance plan
Apply CSDM, scope the service, write the governance plan, then build CIs
Build CIs, write the governance plan, scope the service, then apply CSDM
questions.explain: The capstone scopes the service first (Lesson 23), builds the real CIs and relationships (Lesson 24), applies CSDM mapping and validates data quality (Lesson 25), and closes with governance (Lesson 26).
